title: Move him now
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the acute medical unit. Mr Hall, 60, was admitted with breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain. His CT pulmonary angiogram, requested to look for a pulmonary embolism, has just been reported, but no one has looked at it yet.

The bed manager is pressing for beds, and the medical registrar asks you to transfer him to a general ward now.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Review the CT report yourself straight away.
options.brief: Quick, and may settle the question.
options.detailed: Reading the report takes a minute and may show whether anything needs doing before transfer. It ranks second because the registrar should know too.

options.text: Make sure the receiving ward knows the CT result and any plan.
options.brief: Safe handover if he does move.
options.detailed: Whatever happens, the ward team must know the result. It ranks third because reviewing it comes first.

options.text: Transfer him as asked, as the registrar has made the decision.
options.brief: He may move without a significant result being acted on.
options.detailed: The registrar may not know the report is back. Transferring him without anyone looking at it could delay treatment, and is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Refuse to transfer him anywhere until the consultant has been in to see him.
options.brief: Disproportionate when the report can be reviewed in minutes.
options.detailed: Your concern is right, but a quick review solves it, and refusing outright may cause conflict.

options.text: Tell the registrar the CT report is back, and ask to review it first.
options.brief: The result may change his management.
options.detailed: If the scan shows a pulmonary embolism, he may need treatment before moving. Reviewing it first takes moments.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you raise a concern with a senior before an action that might be unsafe, without being obstructive.
explanation.keyDetails: The CT report is back but unread. The registrar may not know. There is pressure on beds.
explanation.reasoning: [E] informs the registrar, [A] reviews the result, and [B] makes sure the ward knows. [D] is obstructive, and [C] risks a missed result.
explanation.competing: Some would read the report first. That's reasonable; the key puts telling the registrar first because the decision is theirs, and they may simply not know.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 3, raising concerns with seniors about patient safety.
